detail.longDescription: I am working on a Python word-frequency counter. I want to keep contractions and hyphenated words together ( don't , check-in ), but treat a double hyphen as a separator. I tried using re.sub(r"^\W+|\W+$", "", word) to remove surrounding punctuation, but it doesn't split punctuation inside a token. Here is my current code: import re text = "Don't forget the check-in! What about word--word?" counts = {} for word in text.lower().split(): word = re.sub(r"^\W+|\W+$", "", word) counts[word] = counts.get(word, 0) + 1 print(counts) Actual output: {"don't": 1, "forget": 1, "the": 1, "check-in": 1, "what": 1, "about": 1, "word--word": 1} Expected output: {"don't": 1, "forget": 1, "the": 1, "check-in": 1, "what": 1, "about": 1, "word": 2} My current code separates words using text.lower().split() , which splits the text at spaces. However, this keeps word--word together instead of treating the double hyphen as a separator. How can I modify my tokenization so that single internal hyphens and apostrophes are preserved, while double hyphens separate words?
